Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

the Ides noun

the thirteenth or fifteenth day of the Roman month

also Ides, Ides of March

classical

Hor. C. 4.11.14–16
Cic. Att. 6.9.4: Īdibus Octōbribus
Traupman 78–79

Īdūs, Īduum f. pl.

noun, fourth declension, plural · Declension on Wiktionary

the Ides, the 13th of the month (the 15th in March, May, July and October)

About the middle of the month: Horace’s Ides “split” April (C. 4.11.16). The month’s adjective agrees with it: Īdūs Mārtiae, the Ides of March, 15 March, the day Caesar was killed; Īdibus Octōbribus, on 15 October. The days before are counted back to it: prīdiē Īdūs Jānuāriās, 12 January.

Examples

  • Īdūs tibi sunt agendae, quī diēs mēnsem Veneris marīnae findit Aprīlem

    you are to keep the Ides, the day that splits April, the month of sea-born Venus (Maecenas’ birthday)Hor. C. 4.11.14–16

  • Īdibus Octōbribus hās dedī litterās

    I sent this letter on the Ides of OctoberCic. Att. 6.9.4

See also the Kalends, the Nones, month, calendar.
